description.p: CrossMacro is an open-source, cross-platform mouse and keyboard macro recorder, editor, and automation tool for Linux, Windows, and macOS. Record clicks, movement, scrolling, and keyboard input, then edit and replay macros with configurable speed, pauses, loops, repeat counts, delays, global hotkeys, or schedules.

Linux-first Wayland and X11 support provides compositor-aware cursor positioning and daemon-backed or direct-device input paths. CrossMacro uses absolute mouse positioning when the active session exposes a compatible cursor-position protocol and falls back to relative input when that capability is unavailable. It also combines text expansion, screen-reading commands, native PNG image recognition, profiles, themes, a GUI, and a scriptable CLI in one application.

ul.li: Record and replay mouse and keyboard macros with configurable timing and pause/resume control
Edit macros with undo/redo, action reordering, coordinate modes, variables, loops, conditionals, and text input
Bind macros to global hotkeys with toggle or hold-to-run modes
Schedule macros at specific times or intervals, including one-time, weekly, custom weekday, and randomized intervals
Expand text from global shortcuts with configurable typing methods
Read screen pixels and search native PNG templates for image-based workflows
Control playback speed from 0.1x to 10x, loops, repeat counts, and fixed or randomized repeat delays
Save, load, sequence, and replay .macro files, then switch between profiles
Customize themes and use the desktop GUI, CLI, or GUI-less runtime on Linux Wayland/X11, Windows, and macOS
Use customizable global controls with F8 recording, F9 playback, and F10 pause as the defaults

description.p: CrossMacro treats Wayland and X11 as first-class Linux targets and selects compositor-aware positioning and daemon-backed or direct-device input according to the active session's capabilities.
On GNOME, a Shell Extension can be installed on first run. A logout/login may be required for the extension to take effect.

If permissions are missing, the app offers Quick Setup on launch. Quick Setup opens a standard system authorization prompt to enable direct device access for the current user session. If setup cannot complete, use the direct-device troubleshooting instructions in the project README.

description.p: CrossMacro 1.4.0 is a major automation release for Linux. It adds visual automation, Linux window control, structured scripting, a substantially expanded CLI, local MCP integration, higher-fidelity input handling, custom themes, and extensive Wayland and portable-package improvements.

ul.li: Added reusable image assets and image-based actions that can find an image, wait for it to appear, and use the result in later macro steps. Image automation is available in the editor, scripts, CLI, runtime, and saved macros.
Added automatic image matching with a 0.95 confidence threshold, time-bounded colour and image polling, image-click actions, and clearer immediate versus waiting screen commands.
Improved visual automation on multi-monitor desktops with scale-aware matching, transparency and valid-pixel handling, and reliable capture of regions that span multiple displays.

Improved Wayland screen reading with native capture and clipboard backends across the GUI, CLI, and headless runtime; improved PipeWire and Portal capture; common SDR format support; cached frames; multi-monitor selection; and clearer diagnostics.

Added Linux window control for KDE Plasma, GNOME Shell, Hyprland, Niri, and Sway. Macros and CLI commands can list, find, wait for, focus, close, move, resize, center, maximize, fullscreen, float, and move supported windows between workspaces.
Added focused-window shortcut rules that match a window class, title, or process, with a visual picker, CLI support, and persistent settings.
Made window automation degrade safely: unavailable backends are skipped and unsupported controls are hidden instead of causing startup failures.

Added Raw and Logical relative mouse-recording modes. Raw mode records device deltas, while Logical mode records desktop-pixel movement; both are available through settings, recording, the editor, CLI, and saved macros.

Improved relative playback by keeping raw device deltas out of logical cursor settling, re-anchoring logical movement after manual cursor changes, and starting relative editor moves from the current cursor position.

Preserved microsecond macro timing and added motion-fidelity controls for more deterministic relative playback, safer cursor settling, repeated-target handling, and confirmation before rapidly repeating low-delay macros.
Improved Linux input reliability by reporting partial device writes, safely reusing virtual devices, preserving evdev timestamps, and resuming daemon capture after a keyboard or mouse is reconnected.
Added structured script actions for shell commands, clipboard operations, and current mouse-position variables, plus arithmetic with mul, div, and expressions in repeat, for, if, and while arguments.

Shell steps run as the current user in native Linux and AppImage packages. Flatpak shell steps run in a nested networkless sandbox that cannot access host commands, input devices, or the desktop session bus.
Added clipboard get, set, and selected-text capture steps, with safer clipboard error handling and support for using current mouse coordinates in later actions.
Added selected-text capture in the editor, variable mouse coordinates, inline macro testing, and more reliable action editing, undo behaviour, raw-key actions, and random delays.
Added user-defined JSON themes, a themes-folder shortcut, safe theme refresh behaviour that keeps the active theme selected, debounced settings writes, and reduced text-expansion trigger polling.
Added CLI commands for profiles, text expansions, settings, schedules, shortcuts, screenshots, clipboard access, window control, screen reading, direct input, and runtime automation.
The CLI can export screenshots, use native capture services, automate windows, run colour and image actions, and report coordinate modes and backend capabilities.
Added a secure local Model Context Protocol server for controlled AI-assisted CrossMacro workflows, with operation-specific permissions and file-path policies.
Saved loaded macro sessions per profile and improved support for Bazzite and Linux environments with directory-backed identities.

Flatpak and AppImage now select direct input devices predictably on Wayland instead of probing the host daemon. Both retain temporary Quick Setup when input permissions are needed, including a command-line setup flow with clearer authorization guidance.
Flatpak screen reading uses the XDG Desktop Portal and PipeWire, while AppImage follows the native Wayland capture path.

Updated Linux launchers and package integration across Flatpak, AppImage, DEB, RPM, Arch, and Nix. Development snapshots are now available through the crossmacro-git AUR package. Linux daemon authorization and setup now support NSS, Active Directory, LDAP, SSSD, Userborn, and other directory-backed group identities.

Improved runtime recovery after daemon restarts, automatic text-expansion capture recovery after transient failures, duplicate-startup protection, profile persistence, and the installation, platform, CLI, MCP, man-page, and troubleshooting documentation.

description.p: CrossMacro 1.3.1 implements Native AOT compilation, major CLI performance optimizations, and Linux uinput stabilization fixes.

ul.li: Added Native AOT compilation support for CLI and UI packages, eliminating the .NET runtime dependency and dramatically reducing binary size, startup latency, and memory footprint.
Optimized Linux virtual uinput device creation and stabilization using dynamic sysfs and ioctl calls, dropping sequential run delays.
Optimized CLI startup by lazily evaluating capability probes and conditionally bypassing profile initialization, saving multiple redundant disk I/O operations on macro runs.
Fixed a desktop entry filename casing issue across Linux packages to ensure standard application launcher compliance.
Fixed a potential race condition (ENOENT) during evdev hardware device scanning when a temporary virtual uinput node is destroyed.
Replaced the IsCapturing boolean with EditorCaptureMode enum in the UI editor to support rich macro recording states.

description.p: CrossMacro 1.3.0 adds screen-reading capabilities, profile management, and input simulation enhancements.

ul.li: Added pixelcolor, waitcolor, and pixelsearch commands for color-based automation.
Added built-in color picker and region capture controls for editor actions.
Added support for native screen capturing backends.
Added profile management to easily save, load, and switch configuration profiles.
Added Fast and Compatible (Key-by-Key) method selector for Direct Typing text expansion to resolve character skipping.
Added scheduler safeguards to prevent burst-firing of macros after system stalls.
Improved Linux AppImage and Flatpak diagnostics to reliably detect missing input recording permissions upfront.

description.p: CrossMacro 1.2.1 improves text expansion editing and updates GNOME Shell integration metadata.

ul.li: Added multiline text input and expansion support for text expansion entries and editor text actions.
Added GNOME Shell 50 and 51 extension metadata support for newer GNOME environments.

description.p: CrossMacro 1.2.0 improves Linux coordinate recording and playback, diagnostics, input reliability, and package runtime behavior.

ul.li: Improved Linux coordinate recording and playback with clearer absolute and relative coordinate handling.
Expanded Linux daemon, socket, input backend, and doctor diagnostics with clearer startup notifications and troubleshooting details.
Improved direct input capture edge cases, unavailable backend reporting, horizontal scroll recording, and stale daemon event handling.
Added Niri keyboard layout detection for better Wayland desktop integration.
Improved Linux package runtime reliability and metadata for this release.

description.p: CrossMacro 1.1.0 improves everyday automation with a better editor, smoother text expansion, randomized timing controls, stronger Linux integration, and more reliable packages.

ul.li: Added loaded macro playlists, editor filtering, multi-select controls, clearer toolbar actions, bundled icons, and more reliable editor selection behavior.
Added clipboard-free text expansion, faster direct typing, safer paste insertion, and improved clipboard behavior across native sessions, Flatpak, and X11.
Added randomized playback loop delays, schedule intervals, and shortcut repeat delays.
Improved localization coverage for tabs, editor text, runtime states, placeholders, and language settings.
Improved Linux support with Niri and COSMIC detection, batched input simulation, stronger permission handling, clearer setup guidance, and GNOME warning replay.
Improved existing Flatpak integration with better host clipboard handling and cleaner build inputs.
Improved CLI and headless automation with cleaner JSON output and more reliable daemon detection.
Improved release packaging with stricter validation, refreshed package metadata, Avalonia 12, and compact portable Windows packages.

description.p: CrossMacro 1.0.1 delivers major Linux workflow improvements for scripting and Wayland environments.

ul.li: Fixed a Linux mutex contention issue that could cause intermittent daemon synchronization failures.
Added Wayfire Wayland compositor support for absolute pointer position integration.
Added the current-position action for using live cursor coordinates in automation flows.
Expanded the script engine with structured control flow: if, for, while, continue, and break.

description.p: This release improves Linux packaging reliability and refreshes the application metadata for the 0.9.9 release.
This release adds full Flatpak support with Wayland compatibility.
